chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys the shares of the butchers before the share is drawn out. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not buy anything until he knows from where the share comes out. So if he buys something, he has the choice (to accept or reject it) when it comes out.'

key_terms.الْقَصَّابِينَ: The butchers (specifically referring to the practice of drawing lots for meat cuts)
key_terms.بِالْخِيَارِ: Has the choice / option (to accept or reject)
key_terms.سِهَامَ: Shares (in a lottery or drawing context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying lottery shares before the winning item is drawn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the rules of *qirash* (lottery) by specifying that purchasing shares before the source is known introduces excessive uncertainty (*gharar*), rendering the transaction voidable. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the initial purchase is not strictly invalid, the buyer retains the right of option (*khiyar*) to reject the specific item once the draw is complete, highlighting the Shia juristic emphasis on clarity of subject matter in sales contracts. This ruling underscores the practical application of avoiding ambiguity in commercial transactions to ensure fairness and prevent dispute.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Zayd Al Shahham who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who buys the shares of the butchers prior to the shares are allotted. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not buy anything until he knows from were the shares were drawn. So if he were to buy like this he has the choice to buy or not to (buy it), when the share comes out’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Zayd al- Shahham who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who bought the shares of butchers before the shares were taken out.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Nothing can be purchased until it is known where the shares come. If he buys like this he has the choice to buy or not to buy it.’”
